title: QBR FinOps Action Matrix & Spend Playbook
summary: A practical, working worksheet for preparing Customer Success QBRs that focus on usage economics: token spend, rate limits, budget alerts, and renewal-triggered actions. This is intentionally rough — use as a living artifact to capture anomaly investigations, suggested action items, and operational runbooks for finance + CS during renewal conversations.
purpose: Provide a concise matrix mapping spend/risk signals to owners, immediate actions, and next-quarter negotiation levers.
Capture reproducible queries, alert text, and comms templates to speed QBR prep.
Make it easy to highlight potential overages, rate-limit impacts, and budgeting recommendations for renewals.
sections:
1) Key metrics to surface in the QBR
   - 30/60/90-day token burn (total and per-route)
   - Tokens per successful request (median / p95)
   - Peak concurrent RPS and any rate-limit-triggered 429 spikes
   - Embedding vs. generation spend split
   - Cache hit rate (prefix/KV caching) and estimated $ saved
   - Forecasted monthly spend under current growth trends

2) Quick action matrix (use during QBR to assign next steps)
   - Severity: Advisory | Elevated | Critical
   - Signal examples:
       Advisory: steady >10% month-over-month token growth; occasional 429s during peak user hours
       Elevated: sustained >25% MoM growth OR >3% of requests experiencing retries due to 429s
       Critical: sudden one-day spike >200% baseline OR monthly forecast > contracted budget +15%

   - Matrix rows (format: Severity — Who — Immediate action — Runbook link / Notes)
       Advisory — CSM (Marisol) — Add token trend slide; suggest batching review with product — "Check batching metrics; propose 1-2 batching knobs"
       Elevated — Solutions Eng (Aman Shah) — Open incident ticket; enable short-term rate limit increase (if policy allows) and schedule optimization audit — "Audit KV cache settings + route isolation"
       Critical — Account Exec + FinOps (Priya Patel) — Trigger renewal financial review; propose short-term overage contract or immediate Dedicated capacity quote — "Escalate to sales ops; prepare revised MRR impact"

3) Reproducible queries and formulas (copy into internal analytics)
   - SQL example (tokens per route per day):
       SELECT route, date_trunc('day', ts) AS day, sum(tokens) AS tokens_daily, count(1) AS requests, round(sum(tokens)::numeric/count(1),2) AS tokens_per_req
       FROM analytics.tokens
       WHERE ts BETWEEN '{{start}}' AND '{{end}}'
       GROUP BY 1,2
       ORDER BY day DESC;

   - Forecast formula (simple linear):
       next_month = this_month + (this_month - last_month)
       include note: use rolling 7-day growth rate for noisy workloads

4) Budget alert thresholds (suggested defaults, tune per account)
   - Info: forecast > 80% of budget -> "Review"
   - Warning: forecast > 95% of budget or monthly run rate > contracted monthly -> "CSM outreach"
   - Critical: forecast > 110% -> "Finance + Legal notification; propose overage or early renewal"

   - Example alert text (Slack/email snippet):
       "[ACTION] Account: {{account_name}} exceeded 95% of monthly budget. Forecasted month-end spend: ${{forecast}} (Contracted: ${{budget}}). CSM: @marisol — please coordinate triage. See dashboard: {{dash_url}}"

5) Rate-limit playbook
   - If 429 rate emerges:
       - Confirm whether token-based throttling or concurrency limits are causing 429s (check per-route latency and queue metrics).
       - Short-term: reduce client concurrency, enable client-side exponential backoff (sample code), or temporarily increase tiered rate limit if contract permits.
       - Medium-term: identify high-cost routes and propose route-level isolation + dedicated model variant.

   - Client-side backoff snippet (pseudocode):
       retry_with_backoff(attempt):
         sleep = base * (2 ** attempt) + jitter
         if attempt > max: raise

6) Renewal triggers & negotiation plays (tie to usage signals)
   - If 3 consecutive months of >20% MoM growth: recommend proactive renewal discussion with tier upgrade proposal.
   - If usage volatile but predictable (burst-driven): propose committed burst capacity with overage carve-outs.
   - If embeddings >50% of spend and stable: propose embedding-batch discounts or single-model pinning to reduce per-token cost.

7) Example slide bullets for QBR (one-liners)
   - "Token spend grew 18% MoM driven by increased nightly batch jobs; average tokens/request up 12%."
   - "Peak hour 429s observed on /generate-chat; proposed short-term rate bump + route split to keep SLAs."
   - "Forecast shows potential +13% overrun next month—recommend 3-month burst commitment to cap unit costs."

8) Investigation notes (living log) — use this area during prep
   - 2025-02-12: Noticed daily batch on account 'Acme-Apps' doubling tokens after dataset refresh; flagged to SE.
   - 2025-02-18: Solutions Eng (Aman) reduced top-k sampling on test route — tokens/request dropped 9% in 48h.
   - 2025-02-25: Customer agreed to enable KV caching for recommendations; estimated savings $1.2k/mo.

9) Open questions / follow-ups
   - Are we comfortable with the default budget alert thresholds for mid-market customers? (action: Marisol)
   - Should we include a standardized "cost impact" line on renewal one-pagers to simplify negotiations? (action: Priya)

10) Linked artifacts and runbooks
   - Confluence playbook: https://confluence.internal.redwood/cs/qbr-finops-playbook
   - Jira tickets: FINOPS-412, CS-987 (investigation tickets)
   - Dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.com/account-spend?acct={{account_id}}
notes_to_self: Keep this sheet lean during QBRs — move long investigations to a dedicated incident doc.
Copy-paste SQL snippets into analytics ticket when sharing with Eng/Ops.
